tests: the reflexive oʻz- takes a possessive suffix agreeing with the subject (siz … oʻzingizni / *oʻzimni)
some verbs fix the case of their object: qoʻrqmoq takes the ablative, ishonmoq the dative (itdan qoʻrqadi / *itni qoʻrqadi)
the recipient of a ditransitive verb takes the dative, not a second accusative (unga … beradi / *uni … beradi)
an object referring to the subject must be the reflexive oʻz-, not a pronoun (biz oʻzimizni / *bizni boshqaramiz)
stem-final q/k becomes gʻ/g before a vowel-initial possessive suffix (oʻrtogʻim / *oʻrtoqim)
hech (hech kim, hech qachon, hech narsa) needs a negated verb (hech kim kelmadi / *keldi)
coordinated 1st/2nd-person past verbs: the first verb keeps its tense-person ending, not bare -gan (bordik va … boʻldik / *borgan va … boʻldik)
verbs like kerak, boshlamoq, qaror qilmoq take the -ish nominalization, not -gan (murojaat etish kerak / *etgan kerak)
the verb agrees in person with the subject pronoun (biz … egamiz / *egaman)
an agent phrase with tomonidan needs a passive verb (vazir tomonidan tayinlangan / *tayinlagan)
a relative clause before a noun uses a participle, not a finite past verb (obod qilgan joy / *obod qildi joy)
har bir takes a singular noun (har bir sinf / *har bir sinflar)
a noun after a numeral stays singular (uchta kitob / *uchta kitoblar)
keyin and beri take the ablative -dan (urushdan keyin / *urushga keyin)
a possessive suffix agrees in person with the genitive pronoun (mening kitobim / *mening kitobing)
after stem-final q/k the dative is -qa/-ka, not -ga (qishloqqa / *qishloqga)
